title: Jayesh Suryavanshi · Writing
description: Technical studies and field notes on machine learning, LLM agents, and the models I take apart.

items.title: The simulator was the experiment
items.summary: I built a reinforcement learning environment for budgeted fraud investigation and trained a policy that beat every baseline, including a rule I wrote in ten minutes. On the real regime break a one-line heuristic beat it by 3.6x. Five results in the project were wrong before they were right.

items.title: The wrong opponent
items.summary: Jev ships with two headline multipliers and neither one names its opponent. Arithmetic on TypeSafe's own published table shows they are two different opponents, one of which is more accurate than Jev. Sixteen configurations on that chart and not one small model.

items.title: The browser is a peripheral
items.summary: Claude Code can drive Chrome. The documentation covers what it can do and stays quiet on how. Reading the shipped binary, the extension bundle and the MCP server's own session logs turns up five hops, two transports, a coordinate frame that disagrees with its own declared scale, and one surprise about where your page text goes.

items.title: The empty classroom
items.summary: A deep learning professor at IISc Bangalore put down his prepared lecture and spent the hour asking his students why they still come to class. He is also the one automating the answer away: no more research assistants, his own learning moved to an LLM, and a skill on his company's marketplace built to teach in his voice.

items.title: The unmapped majority
items.summary: Most geotagged-social pipelines quietly map the 1-2% of posts that carry exact coordinates and call it 'the geography.' Count the coverage first and a different picture appears. A worked example with GeoSocialX: on a realistic 5,000-post city pull, 84% have no location, place-resolution recovers 10x more than exact coordinates alone, and the honest move is to report the hole.

items.title: Informative but subsumed
items.summary: What news text really adds to unrest forecasting, measured properly: 336M events, 55 countries, leakage-controlled out-of-time backtests, and a signal ladder from tone counts to neural headline embeddings. The semantics of news are already in the event record.

items.title: Inkling, up close
items.summary: A close technical read of Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling: a 975B-parameter open-weights multimodal MoE. What's actually new in the architecture, where it really lands on benchmarks, the interaction-models system it was built for, and how to fine-tune it on Tinker.
